title: 1 · How the fidel works
blurb: Read a fidel character as a consonant plus a vowel, and notice what the spelling does not show.

title: 2 · Fidel rows: ሀ to ቸ
blurb: Read the rows from ሀ through ቸ, and keep the ejective ቀ apart from a plain k.

title: 3 · Fidel rows: ኀ to ዠ
blurb: Read the rows from ኀ through ዠ, and treat the four h letters as one sound.

title: 4 · Fidel rows: የ to ፐ, and the ejectives
blurb: Read the last rows, and hear ጠ, ጨ, ጰ and ጸ as their own consonants.

title: 5 · Letters that sound the same, and reading words
blurb: Read homophone letters and a -wa form, and hear a long consonant the spelling hides.

title: 6 · Greetings: አንተ, አንቺ and እርስዎ
blurb: Greet a man, a woman, or a stranger, and say thank you.

title: 7 · Introducing yourself
blurb: Give your name, ask a man, a woman, or a stranger theirs, and keep ነው in the sentence.

title: 8 · Pronouns and ነው
blurb: Match each pronoun to its own form of is, are, and am.

title: 9 · The and plurals
blurb: Mark a specific noun with the definite ending, and make a plural with -ኦች.

title: 10 · This, that, and the classroom
blurb: Point to a book or a person and say this or that, matching masculine and feminine.

title: 11 · Question words
blurb: Ask what, who, where, when, how and how many, with no helper verb.

title: 12 · Numbers
blurb: Count to ten, say twenty and a hundred, and keep the noun singular.

title: 13 · Possessive endings
blurb: Say my house and your house, with a different ending for a man, a woman and a stranger.

title: 14 · Having: አለኝ
blurb: Say what you have and what you do not have, with the thing first.

title: 15 · በ-, ከ-, ለ-, ወደ
blurb: Say where you are from, where you are, who something is for, and where you are headed.

title: 16 · The past, and the object -ን
blurb: Say where you went and what you drank, including the object ending.

title: 17 · Present and future
blurb: Say where you go and what you drink, for now and for later.

title: 18 · Negatives
blurb: Say you did not go and you do not go, by wrapping the verb.

title: 19 · The infinitive and wanting
blurb: Say you want coffee or want to go, with the thing first and the right ending.

title: 20 · Commands and please
blurb: Tell a man, a woman, or a stranger to come, sit, or go, and say please.

title: 21 · Ethiopian time and days
blurb: Ask the time, use the manual's Ethiopian clock pairs, and name the days.

title: 22 · Prices at the market
blurb: Ask the price and the bill in birr, and answer with ነው.

title: 23 · Likes, and kind remarks
blurb: Say what you like, and give a kind remark that matches the person.

title: 24 · Family
blurb: Name parents and siblings, and match the ending to a man, a woman, or እርስዎ.

title: 25 · At a restaurant
blurb: Order a dish and a drink in Addis Ababa, and ask for the bill.

title: 26 · Directions
blurb: Ask where the hotel is, and say right, left, and straight.
